sentences.text: Pisanosaurus was a small, ground-dwelling herbivore that could reach about 1 meter in length and stood roughly 30 centimeters tall.

The skeleton possessed an open hip socket, a feature shared with many dinosaurs, but the exact orientation of the pubis bone remains uncertain in skeletal reconstructions, with some projections placing it downward and forward in a propubic condition similar to most saurischian dinosaurs.
The only known skeleton was discovered in 1962 by Galileo Juan Scaglia and later described by Argentine paleontologist Rodolfo Casamiquela in 1967.
The genus name Pisanosaurus honors the Argentine paleontologist Juan Arnaldo Pisano and combines it with the Greek word saurus meaning lizard.
Its diet likely consisted of ferns, horsetails, and giant conifers.
It is hypothesized that the large carnivore Herrerasaurus may have preyed on Pisanosaurus.
The scientific classification of Pisanosaurus has been debated for over 40 years.
A 2008 study identified Pisanosaurus as the earliest and most primitive member of the ornithischian group.
Two independent studies in 2017 concluded that Pisanosaurus was a silesaurid.
The parent group of Pisanosaurus is Parapredentata.
The animal lived in a warm, humid environment with seasonal heavy rains and volcanic activity on a volcanically active alluvial plain covered by forests.

Recent studies suggest Pisanosaurus might be a non-dinosaurian silesaurid, but this view has not reached a consensus, as the classification depends heavily on the debated evolutionary relationships of silesaurids.
In 1991, Paul Sereno suggested that the Pisanosaurus fossil might be a chimera, a specimen composed of mixed bones from different animals.
